question.text: A PM forecasts interest rates will DECLINE over the next 6 months. To maximise portfolio price appreciation, she should:

explanation.text: The Logic: Bond prices and interest rates move inversely, and duration measures the sensitivity of bond prices to rate changes. The workbook states that for a declining-interest-rate outlook, the manager would increase portfolio duration to maximise returns. The Trap: Decreasing duration, shifting to floaters, or moving to short-term T-bills are all defensive low-duration choices appropriate when rates are expected to rise, not to fall. Note: Per pages 343-344 and page 90 of the workbook, active duration positioning must also consider the fund objective, regulatory and internal guidelines, the assumptions behind the rate view, and the cost of being wrong.
